_meta.indication: Reduction of elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) in patients with open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension.

pivotal_trials.design: Double-masked, randomized, multi-center, active-controlled, parallel study comparing netarsudil 0.02% QD to timolol maleate 0.5% BID
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension with baseline IOP lower than 27 mmHg
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Mean IOP at 08:00, 10:00, and 16:00 at the Week 2, Week 6, and Month 3 Visits (PP population with maximum baseline IOP <25 mmHg)
pivotal_trials.result: In subjects with baseline IOP <25 mmHg (Rhopressa N=113, Timolol N=124), netarsudil QD was non-inferior to timolol; the upper 95% confidence limit for differences in mean IOP was within 1.5 mmHg at all 9 time points and within 1.0 mmHg at 8 of the 9 time points.

pivotal_trials.design: Double-masked, randomized, multicenter, active-controlled, parallel-group study of netarsudil 0.02% QPM compared to timolol maleate 0.5% BID
pivotal_trials.population: Adult subjects with elevated IOP (open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension) with baseline IOP lower than 30 mmHg
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Mean IOP at 08:00, 10:00, and 16:00 at the Week 2, Week 6, and Month 3 Visits
pivotal_trials.n: Randomized to netarsudil QD (N=251), netarsudil BID (N=254), timolol BID (N=251)
pivotal_trials.result: In subjects with baseline IOP <25 mmHg (Rhopressa N=186, Timolol N=187), mean IOP change from baseline was similar between groups; treatment differences favored timolol by up to 1.8 mmHg in subjects with baseline IOP >=25 and <30 mmHg (Rhopressa N=120, Timolol N=130).

key_safety: Most common ocular adverse reaction was conjunctival hyperemia (53%); other common (approximately 20%) reactions were corneal verticillata, instillation site pain, and conjunctival hemorrhage.
target_moa: Netarsudil is a Rho kinase inhibitor (of both ROCK1 and ROCK2 isoforms) believed to reduce IOP by increasing outflow of aqueous humor through the trabecular meshwork route.
modality: Small molecule (new molecular entity), netarsudil ophthalmic solution

advisory_committee.vote: Dermatologic and Ophthalmic Drugs Advisory Committee (10/13/17): efficacy vote 10 YES-0 NO-0 ABSTAIN; benefit-risk vote 9 YES-1 NO-0 ABSTAIN.

basis.text: The application received Standard (not Priority) review.

summary.text: Rhopressa was submitted as a standard-review 505(b) NDA for a new molecular entity, received 2/28/17, reviewed with a Dermatologic and Ophthalmic Drugs Advisory Committee meeting (10/13/17), and approved 12/18/2017 under a conventional (non-accelerated) approval pathway.

citations.quote: submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) for Rhopressa (netarsudil ophthalmic solution) 0.02%.
